rawOutput.title: Use the Product Rule Independently
rawOutput.rationale: This is a problem-solving skill with a small conceptual foundation. Four short sessions first establish what the product rule does through a complete example, then move toward guided use, independent application, and mixed verification. Each session keeps one action prominent and fits the available 15-minute window.

sessions.title: Understand the Product Rule
sessions.objective: Connect the product rule formula to differentiating two multiplied functions.
sessions.amountLabel: One product-rule model and one complete example
contentTargets: The formula (fg)' = f'g + fg' and the role of each term
completionEvidence: Explain why differentiating a product requires two terms.
Apply the formula to one example with all substitutions shown.

sessions.title: Build the Procedure
sessions.objective: Use a consistent sequence to differentiate a product of two functions.
contentTargets: Identifying f, g, f', and g' before substitution
completionEvidence: Construct the four-part setup for one product.
Solve the derivative using the product rule and simplify it.

sessions.title: Apply the Rule Independently
sessions.objective: Differentiate products without relying on a displayed worked solution.
contentTargets: Independent product-rule application with polynomial factors
completionEvidence: Solve two product-rule derivatives independently.
Explain and repair any incorrect term or simplification.

sessions.title: Verify Flexible Use
sessions.objective: Choose and apply the product rule accurately in mixed situations.
sessions.amountLabel: One rule-choice check and one final application
contentTargets: Recognizing when the product rule is required
completionEvidence: Classify expressions by whether they require the product rule.
Solve one final product-rule problem and justify each term.

activities.label: product rule model
activities.title: Why two terms appear
activities.body: Study the model and example, then identify the role of each part.

essentialIdeas: The product rule says the derivative of a product is f'g + fg', so each factor contributes one term.

activities.label: say it back
activities.title: Explain the rule in words
activities.body: In 1 to 3 sentences, explain why a product gives two derivative terms.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product is f'g + fg', so each factor contributes one term.
activities.correctAnswer: Because each factor changes, the derivative splits into two terms: one where the first function is differentiated and one where the second function is differentiated.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both terms and shows that each factor contributes once. If you only say 'multiply the derivatives,' repair that.

activities.label: fix the mixup
activities.title: Correct the common mixup
activities.body: Revise your explanation using the rule beside the mistake.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Thinking the derivative of a product is just f'g' or that only one factor gets differentiated.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product is f'g + fg', so each factor contributes one term.
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative is not just f'g'. The correct rule is f'g + fg', which adds one term from differentiating each factor.
activities.feedback: The repair is to keep both terms. If one factor is left unchanged in your answer, the rule is still incomplete.

activities.label: explain again
activities.title: Explain it again simply
activities.body: Explain the rule again in plain language, without copying the model.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product is f'g + fg', so each factor contributes one term.
activities.correctAnswer: When two functions are multiplied, the derivative has two parts: differentiate the first and keep the second, then keep the first and differentiate the second.
activities.feedback: This should show the relationship, not just repeat the formula. Mention both parts and what each one does.

activities.label: recognize the rule
activities.title: Choose the correct derivative
activities.body: Select the correct derivative form for a product.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product is f'g + fg', so each factor contributes one term.
activities.feedback: The product rule gives two terms because both factors matter. The other choices miss one factor or use a different rule.

activities.label: product rule model
activities.title: The rule in words
activities.body: Read the explanation, then answer the next question from memory.

essentialIdeas: The product rule says the derivative of a product is f'g + fg', so each factor contributes one term.

activities.label: say it back
activities.title: Explain the rule in words
activities.body: In 1 to 3 sentences, explain why a product gives two derivative terms.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product is f'g + fg', so each factor contributes one term.
activities.correctAnswer: Because each factor changes, the derivative splits into two terms: one where the first function is differentiated and one where the second function is differentiated.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both terms and shows that each factor contributes once. If you only say 'multiply the derivatives,' repair that.

activities.label: fix the mixup
activities.title: Correct the common mixup
activities.body: Revise your explanation using the rule beside the mistake.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product is f'g + fg', so each factor contributes one term.
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative is not just f'g'. The correct rule is f'g + fg', which adds one term from differentiating each factor.
activities.feedback: The repair is to keep both terms. If one factor is left unchanged in your answer, the rule is still incomplete.

activities.label: explain again
activities.title: Explain it again simply
activities.body: Explain the rule again in plain language, without copying the model.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product is f'g + fg', so each factor contributes one term.
activities.correctAnswer: When two functions are multiplied, the derivative has two parts: differentiate the first and keep the second, then keep the first and differentiate the second.
activities.feedback: This should show the relationship, not just repeat the formula. Mention both parts and what each one does.

activities.label: recognize the rule
activities.title: Choose the correct derivative
activities.body: Select the correct derivative form for a product.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product is f'g + fg', so each factor contributes one term.
activities.feedback: The product rule gives two terms because both factors matter. The other choices miss one factor or use a different rule.
